title: The new engine hauled to Muileann chrom
summary: An engine of the new kind, bought by Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn from the shipmasters' works at the southern Seann Skell, comes up the old road to Muileann chrom on a low wagon. Twelve horses of Òrd Mhacha draw it for two days, a priest of the order walking at their head, and at the ford below the town he stands in the water until they take it out.

title: The first dubhan tank at Muileann chrom
summary: Comhairle nam Mèinnean's men set an iron tank on stone piers at the end of the long siding at Muileann chrom and fill it from barrels carted up from the southern Seann Skell. It is the first dubhan tank Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn owns. The families of the yard rows complain of the reek, which clings to cloth.

title: Eachann mac Ruairidh learns the dubhan engine
summary: Eachann mac Ruairidh, a driver of the yard families at Muileann chrom, alone puts his name to Comhairle nam Mèinnean's notice asking for a man to learn the new engine. Two fitters of the southern Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell teach him, one of them a Tuathach of Caol mhòr, Will Garside. In a month he drives it to An Sloc Mòr and back without them.

title: The lamp-makers at the fence
summary: As the first dubhan train of Slighe a' Ghuail passes Muileann mhin on its way to Cathair dhearg, the lamp-makers of Comann nan Lòchran come out of their shops and stand along the fence of the last field in their aprons to watch it go by. One of them holds up a new dubhan lamp, unlit.

title: An old driver will not ride
summary: At dusk on the day of the first dubhan train, Ruairidh mac Eachainn, who drove coal engines on the line for forty years, is asked by his son to ride the new engine to the points and back. He refuses, saying he will not ride behind a fire he cannot see into, and walks home to the yard rows.

title: A fireman struck from the roll
summary: In an t-Ògmhios Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn takes a second fireman off its roll at Muileann chrom and puts no one in his place, the dubhan engine needing none and the trains from An Sloc Mòr growing fewer. The man, a fireman of nineteen years, goes down to the river landing to seek work on the boats.

title: A boy of the yard rows killed
summary: Ailean mac Mhathain, fourteen, of the yard families at Muileann chrom, is crushed between two dubhan tank-wagons being moved by rope and pinch-bar to make room for a second tank. Comhairle nam Mèinnean's clerk enters his death in the yard book as an accident in the changeover. The rows bury him in their corner of the burial ground below the mill.

title: A salt-master of Àth bheag buys a lorry
summary: In the autumn a salt-master of Àth bheag buys a lorry from the works at the southern Seann Skell. It comes up the coast road on its own wheels with a fitter driving and a barrel of dubhan roped behind the seat. The drovers of the east coast go down to the ford of the Abhainn dhubh to look at it.

title: Salt of Àth bheag sent west by Slighe a' Ghuail
summary: The salt-master's lorry brings a second load of salt to the yard at Muileann chrom, and Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn sends it on to Cathair dhearg in a covered wagon behind the empty dubhan tanks. It is the first load the dubhan engine carries towards the capital that is not dubhan, and the first freight it pulls that pays.

title: The last ox-drove on the eastern salt road
summary: In am Faoilleach the last ox-drove goes out of Àth bheag with salt on the old drove road past Baile ìseal: four carts and twenty-four beasts, driven by Murchadh Bàn and his two grandsons. It takes five days to reach the inland towns in the rain. On his return the old man sells the oxen at the ford and buys no others.

title: A dubhan tank at An Sligeanach Fad' às
summary: Over the winter the landlord of An Sligeanach Fad' às, of the drover families of Achadh mhòr, sets an iron tank on stone piers in the forecourt with a hand-pump beside it, and sells dubhan by the gallon to the lorries on the southern road. By spring he has sold more fuel off it than beds.

title: The last ox-sale at An Sligeanach Fad' às
summary: Meeting in the second hall of An Sligeanach Fad' às, the drover families of Achadh mhòr agree to sell their teams and take lorries from the southern Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell against the price, the rest to be paid from the grain over three years. The oxen are sold in the inn's yards that afternoon, the last beasts to fill them.

title: The blessing for a horse said over an engine
summary: Before the first dubhan train leaves the yard at Muileann chrom the priest of Macha says over it the blessing for a horse setting out on a long road, since none has been made for an engine.

title: Pilgrims carried up to Caol shean by engine
summary: A river-boat fitted with a dubhan engine carries pilgrims up to the landing at Caol shean against the current in half a day, where the rowed boats took two; the boatmen of the landing let it moor without a word said.
